heading: CONCERNING

translated_text:
REGIONAL HOUSE OF REPRESENTATIVES

OF PENUKAL ABAB LEMATANG ILIR REGENCY

AND

REGENT OF PENUKAL ABAB LEMATANG ILIR

DECIDES:

To Establish: REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN.

heading: CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: 1. Regency is Penukal Abab Lematang Ilir Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Regent as an element of the regency government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.

3. Regent is the Regent of Penukal Abab Lematang Ilir. 4. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and the Regency Regional House of Representatives in the administration of government affairs that are the authority of the regency.
5. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb. 6. Woman is a human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Fulfillment of Children's Rights is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological, and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of a person's freedom unlawfully. 9. Victim is a woman and/or child who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the territory of Penukal Abab Lematang Ilir Regency. 10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutor's office, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Prevention is activities carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children. 13. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
14. Empowerment is the strengthening of women victims of violence to be able to work and work independently after they are recovered and provided with health and social rehabilitation services.
15. Health Rehabilitation is an effort to restore the condition of victims including physical, psychological and social health so that victims can carry out their roles again properly and reasonably both in the family and in society.
16. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person who experiences social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
17. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the regional territory to their region of origin.
18. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
19. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence and is integrated with PPT that organizes integrated services for witnesses and/or victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons.

Article 2 The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children is carried out based on the principles of:
a. respect and protection of human rights; b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination;
d. the best interests of the Child;
e. the right to life, survival, and development; f. Empowerment; and g. legal certainty.

Article 3 The Protection of Women and Children aims to: a. guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of Women and Children; b. maintain the integrity of the household so as to realize a harmonious family;
c. prevent violence against Women and Children; d. protect and provide a sense of security for Women and Children;
e. provide services to Women and Children victims of acts of violence;
f. provide protection to reporters and witnesses; and g. carry out empowerment for Women victims of violence.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health Article 8 (1) The implementation of Fulfillment of Children's Rights in the field of health as referred to in Article 5 letter b, the Regency Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health services for children.

2. Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, Children with disabilities, children with special needs, street children, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child laborers, children victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (NAPZA) abuse, Children who are victims of violence, such as neglect, economically and sexually exploited and victims of human trafficking.
3. Exemption from cost burden for Children as referred to in paragraph (2) letter b is for Children from poor families unless otherwise regulated in accordance with the health financing program established by the government.

Article 9 The Regency Government together with the community, family and parents are obliged to ensure that Children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten the continuity of life and/or cause disability.

heading: CHAPTER III

CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

MONITORING AND EVALUATION

Article 27 (1) The Regency Government conducts monitoring to ensure synergy, balance and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, activities for the Protection of Women and Children.

2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus and PPT.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
4. Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of Regional Apparatus implementing policies and activities for the Protection of Women and Children.
5. The Monitoring stages as referred to in paragraph (1) include: a. planning b. policy implementation;
c. program implementation; and d. activities for the Protection of Women and Children every year. Article 28 (1) Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children shall be conducted at the end of each Budget year or when necessary according to needs.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the Protection of Women and Children as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

heading: CONCERNING
translated_text:
CONCERNING

THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children constitutes a violation of human rights, therefore their dignity and honor must be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and disposition without discrimination. The fate of women and children who are victims of violence must be given attention by the regional government. The high number of cases of violence against women and children is often caused by factors that develop in society, for example low economic levels, education, environments located in the industrial sector. Therefore, victims of violence such as this need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality and upholding human rights.

For the empowerment of victims of violence, the district government establishes an Integrated Service Center (PPT) which is a generic term that can be used by various institutions that provide services for victims of violence such as the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A), Safe Houses, Child Social Protection Houses (RPSA), Trauma Center Protection Houses (RPTC), Women's Social Protection Houses (RPSW), Shelters, etc.

The District Government is obligated and responsible to implement efforts to protect women and children through implementing protection policies for women and children applied by the government, establishing policies, programs, and protection activities for women and children, establishing PPT, guaranteeing the implementation of service facilities for victims, seeking effectiveness and efficiency for the victim recovery process, and seeking the creation of cooperation and coordination in efforts to protect women and children.

heading: II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE
translated_text:
II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1 Number 5 In accordance with the Law related to children, a child is any person under the age of 18 years.

Article 2 Letter a Sufficiently clear.

Letter b What is meant by "justice and gender equality" is a process to be fair to men and women and equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, national defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of such development.

Letter c What is meant by "non-discrimination" is that child protection is provided to all children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter d What is meant by "the best interests of the child" is that all actions concerning children carried out by the government, society, legislative bodies, the best interests of the child must be a primary consideration.

Letter e What is meant by "the right to life, survival of the child and development of the child" is as stated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate, as well as rights inherent in the life of the child to obtain health standards, education and an adequate standard of living for the physical, mental, spiritual, moral and social development of the child.

Letter f What is meant by "empowerment" is a process of increasing the role of society to participate in the implementation of protection for women and children who are victims of violence which aims to obtain access and participation in the process of protection for women and children broadly.

Letter g Sufficiently clear.

Article17 Sufficiently clear.

Article18 Lettera What is meant by "physical violence" is an act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.

Letterb What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letterc What is meant by "sexual violence" is an act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse and/or forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letterd What is meant by "neglect" is an act that results in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; the act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or other parties responsible for their care; the act of neglecting a person within the household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Lettere What is meant by "exploitation" is an act that exploits economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; an act with or without the victim's consent including prostitution, forced labor or service, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain material or immaterial benefits; and/or any form of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency.

Letterf What is meant by "other violence" is the threat of violence including: any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that create fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom; and coercion, including: a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article19 Sufficiently clear.

Article20 Sufficiently clear.

Article21 Lettera What is meant by "fast" is immediate action taken without complications or simplified procedures.

Letterb What is meant by "safe and comfortable" is a guarantee of service protection that feels comfortable, undisturbed, and served in a friendly, respectful and appreciative manner.

Letterc What is meant by "empathy" is an act of appreciating, respecting, loving, befriending, and making happy that aims to please and calm the victim's heart.

Letterd What is meant by "non-discrimination" is handling of victims provided to all victims without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Lettere What is meant by "guarantee of confidentiality" is an effort to guarantee certainty for victims that their identity, medical treatment and legal handling will not be disseminated. Letterf What is meant by "easily accessible" is the provision of services and assistance for all people regardless of their social status, so that such services are affordable for the underprivileged or relatively sufficient for the privileged.

Letterg What is meant by "free of charge" is that the activities of providing services and assistance carried out by PPT are not charged to the victim.

Article22 Lettera What is meant by "complaint, consultation, and counseling services" includes initial identification or recording of victims; case identification; and consent for action to be taken.

Letterb What is meant by "assistance services" includes accompanying victims during the examination and health recovery process; accompanying victims during the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court; monitoring the interests and rights of victims in the examination process at the police, prosecutor's office and court; maintaining the privacy and confidentiality of victims from all parties who have no interest, including reporting by mass media; providing a sense of security to victims; and providing continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage.

Letterc What is meant by "medical rehabilitation services" includes first aid to victims; treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics; and referral to health services.

letterd What is meant by "social rehabilitation services" is services provided in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims. The form of service is carried out through social support through spiritual guidance to victims; and psychological recovery of victims. Lettere What is meant by "legal services" is to assist victims in undergoing the judicial process by providing legal consultation that includes information regarding victims' rights and the judicial process; accompanying victims at the investigation, prosecution, and court hearing examination levels and helping victims to fully describe the violence they experienced; and coordinating with fellow law enforcers, volunteer assistants, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

Letterf What is meant by "social reintegration services" is aimed at returning victims to their families and social environment. Social reintegration services are carried out by the Regency Government by coordinating with relevant government and non-government agencies and institutions; and village community institutions and/or local community leaders.
